bibliographic.title: Trust and Ethics in Chatbots: A Framework for Responsible AI Interactions
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sowmya, P., & Vasudeva. (2026). Trust and ethics in chatbots: A framework for responsible AI interactions. IEEE Access. https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3653763

methodology.method_family: ethical framework development with experimental chatbot evaluation
methodology.study_design: framework-based ethical evaluation with comparative performance metrics across chatbot datasets/domains
methodology.sample_description: university chatbot evaluated on intent-pattern variations; additional comparison with healthcare and customer service chatbots
methodology.technology_context: intent-classification chatbots; Ethics by Design for AI (EbD-AI); European Commission Trustworthy AI principles; comparisons with IBM AIF Fairness 360 and Microsoft RAI Toolkit; background discussion of ChatGPT, GPT-4, Bard and LLM ethics audits

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly addresses responsible AI governance for chatbots, including oversight, fairness, accountability, privacy, auditability, explainability, and continuous monitoring, with application contexts in education, healthcare, and customer service. Although the reported empirical evaluation centers on intent-pattern chatbot performance rather than explicit LLM deployment governance, the framework and governance mechanisms align closely with the review scope on conversational AI in sensitive settings.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Full text is needed to confirm whether the evaluated university chatbot is LLM-based or traditional NLP/intent-based, and to verify the extent of healthcare/customer-service comparisons beyond abstract claims.

appraisal.notes: The objective and ethical framing are comparatively clear, and reported metric bands are explicit in the abstract. However, the provided text gives limited detail on sampling, data-collection procedures, analysis methods, and study limitations; the LLM-related audit content may partly reflect prior work rather than the authors' own empirical design.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is coherent and relevant to conversational AI governance, but methodological transparency in the supplied excerpts is limited for sampling, analysis, and validation design, reducing confidence in how strongly the empirical results support governance claims.

coding.theme: Responsible governance framework for ethical chatbot interactions
coding.subtheme: Dataset-intent robustness, trust, fairness, and auditing in regulated chatbot use

synthesis.main_claim: Chatbot ethical behaviour should be ensured through a structured responsible-AI framework that evaluates robustness, fairness, privacy/data governance, and societal well-being, while recommending auditability, explainability, validation, monitoring, and ethical auditing under changing datasets.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes an ethics-oriented framework for chatbot interactions and reports comparative ethical-performance metrics for a university chatbot, with additional domain comparisons and benchmarking against established fairness/RAI toolkits.
synthesis.limitations: The supplied text does not clearly specify sample sizes, full experimental protocol, or detailed limitations of the empirical evaluation; the extent of LLM-specific governance evidence in the authors' own study remains unclear.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as central evidence on ethical governance frameworks, trust/fairness evaluation, and post-deployment monitoring/auditing for chatbots in education, healthcare, and customer-service contexts; triangulate cautiously for LLM-specific operational governance until full-text methods are verified.
